subject: Working with a constrained multivariate normal distribution

messages.author: 216b106619b6f746
messages.subject: Working with a constrained multivariate normal distribution
parts:
Hi

I'm trying to implement a model in which I have vectors alpha which sum
to 0 and come from a multivariate normal distribution. Specifically, if
alpha has N elements then I want the means to be 0 and the covariance
matrix to have 1 on the diagonal and -1/(N-1) everywhere else.

Currently I'm implementing this by introducing a N-1 element vector
alpha_raw which has a multivariate normal distribution and then applying
a suitable linear change of variables (see the model below). I am
interested in values of N around 20. It unfortunately appears that I
need to use very many samples before the covariances look right. for
example sampling the below model with N=20, sigma=1, and the default of
4 chains and 2000 iterations the first row of the covariance matrix of
the sampled alpha is
0.996 -0.019 -0.079 -0.044 -0.066 0.004 -0.059 -0.003 -0.105 -0.074
-0.103 -0.081 -0.051 -0.058 -0.005 -0.100 -0.067 -0.056 -0.003 -0.029

I was wondering if anyone can suggest a better approach that would
require fewer iterations?

My sample model is below, obviously in practice I have something much
more complex.

Best wishes

Alastair Irving

data {
int<lower=1> N;
real<lower=0> sigma;
}

transformed data {
vector[N-1] zeros;
//The matrices we need for sampling and transforming multivariate normals
//we will sample n-1 variables with the covariance matrix cov and then
apply the map J to transform to N variables which sum to 0
matrix[N-1,N-1] cov;
matrix[N,N-1] J;
zeros<-rep_vector(0,N-1);
cov<-(diag_matrix(rep_vector(1,N-1))+rep_matrix(1,N-1,N-1))*N*1.0/(N-1);
J<-append_row(diag_matrix(rep_vector(1,N-1))-1.0/N*rep_matrix(1,N-1,N-1),rep_row_vector(-1.0/N,N-1));
}


parameters {
vector[N-1] alpha_raw;
}

transformed parameters {
vector[N] alpha;
alpha<-J*alpha_raw;
}
model {
alpha_raw ~ multi_normal(zeros,sigma^2*cov);
}

messages.author: 743bbacc59f4b25f
messages.subject: Re: Working with a constrained multivariate normal distribution
parts:
You want to pre-multiply a vector of iid standard normals by a square root of that covariance matrix. This would work out to

transformed data {
  matrix[N,N] cov;
  matrix[N,N] S;
  cov<-(diag_matrix(rep_vector(1,N-1)) +
       rep_matrix(1,N-1,N-1))*N*1.0/(N-1);
  S <- block(eigenvector_sym(cov),
             1, 1, N, N - 1);
  # now scale up by the non-zero singular values
  S <- S * sqrt(N / (N - 1.0));
  # now scale up by sigma
  S <- S * sigma;
}
parameters {
  vector[N] alpha_raw;

}
transformed parameters {
  vector[N] alpha;

alpha <- S * alpha_raw;
}
model {
  alpha_raw ~ normal(0,1);
  # implies alpha ~ multi_normal(0, S * S')
}

Ben
